trainers.instruction: When Luca shouts to his friends, Jamal hears Luca’s voice louder than Priya. Why is this?

feedback.end: The closer you are to the source of a sound, the louder the noise will seem.

instruction.text: Rosa is standing next to the stage. Both musicians are playing at the same volume. Select the musician that Rosa will hear the loudest.

feedback.end: Exactly! The musician with the blue guitar will seem louder to Rosa because he is closer. But how does that work?

instruction.text: Select the vibrations that are coming from the musician at the back of the stage.

feedback.end: These vibrations have further to travel to reach Rosa’s ears. While they travel, the vibrations become more spread out. This means more of their energy will be lost along the way, making the sound quieter for Rosa.

instruction.text: The sounds from the TV and the birds near the open window are the same volume. Select the source of the sound that Maeve can hear the loudest.

feedback.end: To Maeve, the TV will seem louder than the birds in the garden because the vibrations don’t have to travel as far to reach her ears.

instruction.text: Why does the distance travelled have an effect on the volume?

atoms.a: If the radio and the kitten are both producing sound at the same volume, which will Fred hear louder?
atoms.sound: If the radio and the kitten are both producing sound at the same volume. Which will Fred hear louder?

atoms.a: Why will the kitten be quieter?
